11.ai_answer: The equilibrium price will definitely increase, but the effect on equilibrium quantity is ambiguous. The drought decreases supply (shifts supply curve left), which alone would raise price and lower quantity. The cancer-prevention discovery increases demand (shifts demand curve right), which alone would raise both price and quantity. Combined effects: Both shifts push price upward, so price definitely rises. However, the supply decrease pushes quantity down while the demand increase pushes quantity up. The net effect on quantity depends on which shift is larger - if demand increases more than supply decreases, quantity rises; if supply decreases more, quantity falls; if equal, quantity stays the same.

12.ai_answer: When producers expect higher future prices for good A, they will reduce current supply to sell more in the future when prices are higher. This decreases current supply (shifts the supply curve left). With demand unchanged, this leads to a higher equilibrium price today and a lower equilibrium quantity today. Essentially, producers withhold inventory from the current market in anticipation of better returns later, creating scarcity in the present market.
